purpose: Reject a near-duplicate full-session directional-efficiency idea before values and select one economically distinct minute-path mechanism for the next ordered no-return audit.

daily_path_efficiency.name: signed_efficiency_ratio_10
daily_path_efficiency.terminal_evidence: The exact higher ten-session signed path-efficiency direction was already tested and rejected; changing only the sampling frequency is not economic independence.

rejected_before_value_observation.name: intraday_directional_efficiency_ratio_238m
rejected_before_value_observation.proposed_formula: sum(r_j) / sum(abs(r_j)) across the 238 within-half adjacent minute log returns
rejected_before_value_observation.reason: This is the same signed path-efficiency mechanism as terminal daily signed_efficiency_ratio_10 at a different sampling frequency, and it is also a price-only/full-session variant of the terminal afternoon amount-weighted directional-efficiency branch. Frequency and weighting removal do not establish a genuinely independent mechanism.

selected_candidate.name: intraday_diffusive_variation_ratio_238m
selected_candidate.formula: [(pi/2) * sum_h sum_{j=2..119} abs(r_hj) * abs(r_h,j-1)] / [sum_h sum_{j=1..119} r_hj^2], for h in morning and afternoon
selected_candidate.mechanism: The ratio of within-half realized bipower variation to realized variance measures whether quadratic variation is distributed through adjacent continuous moves rather than concentrated in isolated jumps.
selected_candidate.hypothesis: A high close-known ratio indicates smoother continuous price discovery and less isolated shock concentration, which may reduce immediate reversal risk and persist from the next open through the third close.
selected_candidate.economic_distinction: It is sign-blind and amount-free. It measures temporal concentration of absolute return magnitudes, not total volatility, morning-versus-afternoon allocation, positive-versus-negative semivariance, terminal position, sign runs, signed path efficiency, amount timing, or amount-return dependence.
